target_customer: Homeowners and renters, and later property managers, who want to unlock doors from a phone
problem: Physical keys cannot be shared or controlled remotely; Lockitron let people lock and unlock a deadbolt from a phone app.
business_model: Hardware sales of smart lock devices (Lockitron, then Lockitron Bolt) sold direct and later through retailers

founders.name: Cameron Robertson
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder and CEO, no background given

founders.name: Paul Gerhardt
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on YC page and described as Apigy co-founder in press

founders.name: Robert Witoff
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a founder

technical_complexity.rationale: Required custom hardware, a motorized deadbolt mechanism with 60 knob designs, wireless firmware and a mobile app, with manufacturing at small scale.

defensibility.rationale: Locksmith incumbents had distribution; the electronics and app were reproducible and the product had no network effects.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Schlage and Kwikset already sold phone controlled locks by the time Lockitron shipped, and Schlage later partnered with Apigy; Chamberlain bought the product line in January 2019.

market_need_then: Keyless entry and phone control for homes was a new idea in 2009 to 2010; demand later showed in 2012 when pre-orders raised over 2 million in preorders from about 14,700 backers.

branding.domain_note: Used lockitron.com; no purchase story found. LOCKITRON trademark filed by Apigy in 2012, now inactive

identity.logo: Logo incorporates the lock knob, which went through about sixty designs per one source

branding.brand_signature: Rejected by Kickstarter, ran its own pre-order campaign
branding.community_and_virality: Self hosted pre-order campaign drew about 10,000 backers in 24 hours and press coverage of the Kickstarter rejection

brand_strength.rationale: Strong crowdfunding press in 2012 and a recognizable product name, but delivery delays and criticism of the first device limited the brand.

pivots.why: Production of the earlier model stopped over manufacturing and product issues

outcome_analysis: Lockitron started as a hand built phone controlled deadbolt in Bay Area offices and became a crowdfunding hit in 2012 with about 2.3 million in preorders after Kickstarter turned it down. Manufacturing problems and delays hurt the first device, Apigy replaced it with the Bolt in 2015 and Chamberlain bought the Lockitron product line in January 2019. Sources do not state a purchase price.
notes: Competitor list left empty: nothing dated near the 2009 batch found; Schlage and Kwikset phone locks are cited in 2012 and 2013 coverage and are not recorded as competition at founding. The crowdfunding round is recorded as stage other with the 2012 year only; the exact month was not confirmed and seed investors were not found (Seedtable 2.3M seed with estimated investors and CB Insights 20K total are unverified aggregator figures). Site lockitron.com could not be fetched (DNS error). Shutdown of the standalone service on 2020-06-17 comes from aggregators only, unverified. Founder backgrounds not found.
